title: GRUMB v2.0 — Genome-Resolved Urban Microbiome Biosurveillance Framework
description:
GRUMB (Genome-Resolved Urban Microbiome Biosurveillance) is an open-source, SLURM-compatible framework that integrates genome-resolved metagenomics, ecological modeling, and machine learning for predictive biosurveillance and AMR risk assessment.

New in GRUMB v2.0:

  • Integration of machine learning–guided ecological diagnostics
  • Synthetic microbial blending and contamination simulation
  • Entropy-based uncertainty quantification and tipping point detection
  • Directional source–sink dominance mapping
  • Composite ecological risk scoring (entropy, richness, variance)
  • Batch correction using CLR + limma
  • Updated documentation, modular codebase, and reproducible benchmarks

This framework enables genome assembly, MAG recovery, AMR and virulence annotation, and predictive modeling of microbial resilience and contamination risk across ambulances, hospital interiors, sewage, and public transport systems.

Companion paper: Aminu et al., *Microbiome* (2025, under review)

Original publication: Aminu et al., *Bioinformatics* (2024), DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.15505402
